data.title: PR-20 IMPL-01: repair transaction begin/apply with the untrusted hypothesis and the apply-time intent-mutation refusal

data.reason: [INFO] Exact-range security review complete for 157353800066a7edb7a5af419758a466752f1180..6e18c78c67e577b4047f5b56796e5a30a9645d60. No reportable finding. crates/continuum-repair/src/transaction.rs:582-615 fails closed for unknown, unbound, and unavailable failure bindings. Lines 628-656 reject every declared intent-kind change before sealing. Lines 659-690 and 832-885 derive immutable canonical identity and artifact bytes. crates/continuum-repair/src/hypothesis.rs:40-66 keeps hypothesis prose opaque in Debug and confines its current reader to serialization. Failure modes: a future daemon could misbind a crashpack, trust the unchecked candidate seam, omit request bounds, or let prose affect decisions. Edge cases: unknown versus unavailable bindings, intent changes at every list position, control and Unicode prose, every gate profile, and version exhaustion need coverage. Rollback: revert this isolated crate surface, dependencies, fixtures, and dossier registration; no daemon or wire path consumes it. Monitoring: future wiring should count typed begin and apply refusals, request-size refusals, identity collisions, and gate-3 blocks without logging hypothesis text. Validation: future wiring must bound requests, authenticate crashpack visibility, verify snapshot-intent bindings, seal base plus declared changes, and use the production cryptographic hasher. The public SealedCandidate::unchecked_from seam at transaction.rs:455-460 and deferred request bounds at lib.rs:62-71 remain explicit prerequisites, not hidden assurances. Static LGTM does not satisfy any separate risk:critical human gate.
